subject: Private deployment: customer KMS geofencing & subprocessor checklist
messages:
From: Emma Ruiz <emma.ruiz@orchid-health.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwo od.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jan 2028 14:23:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment: KMS, subprocessors, and cross-border flows

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for an on-prem gateway at Orchid Health. Before we move to procurement we need clarity on a few privacy/compliance items so we can brief engineering and legal: 

1) Customer-managed keys: can Orchid be the exclusive custodian for encryption keys (no Redwood access) for model inputs/outputs and logs? If not, what limited operator breakglass controls do you support and how are they scoped/recorded?

2) Subprocessors: please send the current subprocessor list for Private and confirm notification timing for adding new subprocessors. We also need a committed process for vetting and the ability to object for specific subprocessors.

3) Cross-border transfer risk: we need assurance that with our VPC/on-prem configuration no customer content will transit US borders without our consent. If there are any telemetry or managed-control-plane flows, what data types are sent and are they encrypted at rest/in transit?

We can share a redline of our DPA if helpful. Would you prefer a call or a short email doc? We need answers by EOD Tuesday to keep the procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Emma Ruiz
Head of Security and Privacy
Orchid Health

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Emma Ruiz <emma.ruiz@orchid-health.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jan 2028 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: KMS, subprocessors, and cross-border flows

Emma — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned to be explicit since this is a Private deployment + on-prem gateway. High-level answers below; I'll loop legal and infra to provide more granular language and attachments.

1) Customer-managed keys: yes — we support customer-controlled KMS for data-at-rest encryption keys used by the private gateway and customer keystores. We offer two modes: 
  - Customer-hosted KMS: customer runs/presents their own KMS endpoint (recommended for on-prem) and Redwood never stores the root keys.
  - Customer-managed keys in cloud KMS: customer controls CMKs in their cloud provider and grants Redwood runtime access limited to wrapper keys.

Operator breakglass: In both modes we provide an auditable emergency access workflow (breakglass) that requires a multi-party approval (customer operator + Redwood SRE) and is logged to audit trails. We'll attach the playbook and proposed DPA wording.

2) Subprocessors: I'll attach the current list. For Private deployments we limit subprocessors to the minimal set needed for deployment and support (e.g., managed telemetry ingestion, storage replication for backups where applicable). We notify customers 30 days in advance of non-security-critical additions and provide an objection window. Legal will confirm this timing in writing.

3) Cross-border data flow: For on-prem/VPC topology, customer data remains within the customer's network and hosts. Control-plane metadata (deployment health checks, licensing heartbeat) is minimized and, where possible, anonymized. Any control-plane telemetry sent to Redwood is encrypted in transit and stored with customer scoping; we'll mark telemetry categories (diagnostic, billing, usage) in the attached playbook.

I'll follow up with more explicit DPA language and a redlined doc tomorrow morning. If you're ok with a short call, I can schedule a 30-min slot with legal and infra.

Best,
Sofia
Head of Privacy Programs | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: KMS, subprocessors, and cross-border flows

Sofia — quick legal notes for the redline: 

- DPA clause for KMS: propose "Customer retains sole control over encryption keys for Customer Data; Redwood will not access plaintext Customer Data except under the Emergency Access Procedure described in Appendix X, which requires: (i) written request from Customer security admin; (ii) two Redwood approvers; and (iii) audit log publication to the Customer."

- Subprocessor notice: 30 days is fine for non-critical additions; for security-critical subprocessors (e.g., new managed-storage provider) require immediate notice and mutual agreement. Add an objection right with remediation/transition plan.

- Cross-border: include explicit language that control-plane telemetry WILL NOT include Customer PII or model prompts. Diagnostic traces may contain hashed identifiers only, and retention limited to 90 days by default unless customer requests longer.

I'll draft these as tracked changes in the DPA.

-Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jan 2028 10:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: KMS, subprocessors, and cross-border flows

Notes from infra on breakglass and telemetry: 

- Breakglass implementation: for customer-hosted KMS, we never have access to raw keys. For the cloud-CMK mode we can request temporary access tokens scoped to a single recovery operation; these tokens are minted only after the approval flow and are single-use. We should document time-limited sessions and ephemeral credentials.

- Telemetry types: categorize as (A) operational health (instance up/down, GPU metrics), (B) control-plane events (model rollouts, config changes), (C) usage/billing counters (token counts). None of these should contain customer prompt/response content. We can offer a zero-telemetry option for on-prem that disables (A) and (C) and shunts minimal control-plane health into a customer-hosted aggregator.

- Data residency: On-prem is fully resident. For VPC-managed Private, ensure subnet ACLs + egress rules prevent outbound flows; we support VPC endpoints and peering.

I'll help prepare a short operational playbook and a sample audit log schema.

-Rishi
Director, Platform Infra

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Emma Ruiz <emma.ruiz@orchid-health.com>, Orchid Health Legal <legal@orchid-health.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jan 2028 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: KMS, subprocessors, and cross-border flows

Emma — attaching the proposed language and two lightweight attachments (subprocessor list + infra playbook stub). Below are the key DPA callouts we recommend adding to the main DPA and Appendix: 

1) Customer Key Custody (new Section X):
  - "Customer Controls Keys": Customer retains exclusive control over master keys for Customer Data when using Customer-Hosted KMS. Redwood will not possess plaintext keys and will only accept short-lived, scoped tokens for recovery operations as described in Appendix X.
  - Emergency Access Procedure: documented escalation requiring: (1) Customer security admin approval, (2) two Redwood approvers (SRE + Security lead), (3) entry into the immutable audit log sent to customer and retained per retention schedule.

2) Subprocessor Management (Section Y):
  - Current subprocessor list attached (subprocessors_20280110.csv).
  - Notification: 30-day notice for routine additions; immediate notice + joint risk review for security-critical subprocessors.
  - Objection right: customer can object within 15 days; if agreement not reached, Redwood will provide a migration/remediation plan or suspend the subprocessor use for that customer.

3) Data Residency & Telemetry (Section Z):
  - On-prem private gateway: Customer Data (inputs, model outputs, logs) remains on customer infrastructure unless explicit written consent for export.
  - Control-plane telemetry: scope and examples included in kms_operational_playbook_stub.md. By default telemetry excludes raw prompts/responses; hashed identifiers only.
  - Zero-telemetry option: available for regulated deployments; note small loss of remote diagnostics.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_proposal_20280110.pdf (redline), subprocessors_20280110.csv, kms_operational_playbook_stub.md

If this looks OK I can send the redline for signature via DocuSign (link below). If you want changes to the breakglass trigger criteria, tell us which roles need to be part of approvals.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/s/abc123-O-54321
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/54321/deal/54321

Best regards,
Sofia

From: Emma Ruiz <emma.ruiz@orchid-health.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Orchid Health Legal <legal@orchid-health.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jan 2028 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: KMS, subprocessors, and cross-border flows

Thanks Sofia — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. The DPA redline looks good overall; two quick asks before we sign: 

1) Can Redwood shorten the routine-subprocessor notice from 30 days to 15 for our account? Our procurement prefers shorter windows for smaller vendors.
2) For the Emergency Access Procedure, add that any breakglass event requires a post-incident report within 72 hours describing the trigger, actions taken, and key artifacts.

If you can accept those, send the final DocuSign and we will get Legal to countersign today.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Emma
Head of Security and Privacy
Orchid Health
